acceptance: Run official wasm-tools parse then validate --features all in the sole Linux 64-GiB cgroup under the approved finite guardian; retain actual executable/provider/version/argv/rc and all raw output.
Derive the actual generated Wasm final-access binary offset from the official opcode dump. Bind that exact binary SHA/offset in a new result record before the product execution.

Bind fresh product source, target ISA/libc, full compiler/LLVM/CRT/link/loader closure and all relevant runtime translation units. Header-only or historical binaries do not qualify current product behavior.

Require the expected Wasm trap class and final-access function/offset witness. Arbitrary nonzero process exit, unavailable feature, validation rejection, failed linking, native signal without a Wasm trap witness, or the earlier unreachable is a failure or unqualified result.
Record the full Wasm i64 address/index/offset in diagnostics when available. A successful process exit is a failure: it may indicate the high bits were lost.
For i386, record direct ELF32 IA32-compatible kernel execution and qemu-i386 translated execution separately. Neither result implies Windows/FreeBSD hardware trap qualification.
For both products distinguish developer GNU ABI diagnostics from vendored LLVM23 ROS production qualification.

Expand from the first short correctness cell to each supported uwvm-int full/lazy and llvm-jit full/lazy/tiered mode and active exception-policy matrix only after its fresh product/target closure exists.

primary_sources.claim: Core3 load traps when address + offset + access width exceeds the memory byte count.
Core3 table.get traps when the full-width table index is at least the table length.
The memory64 composition gives all Threads memory operations i64 addresses on an i64 memory; the effective address is checked without truncation.
Atomic load follows non-atomic load bounds rules and uses sequential consistency.

semantics.distinction: The memory64+Threads fixture tests the Threads extension composed with Core3 memory64; shared atomics are not claimed to be part of Core3 alone.
semantics.rationale: A 32-bit native pointer or helper ABI must preserve the Wasm i64 address/index until a full-width bounds check. Passing an access at address zero after truncation is a failure.
